brief:
The article examines complications in forming a government within Israel, centered on a power struggle between Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu amid the absence of a decisive parliamentary majority, Shehab Wire reported. Conflicting interests among the Change camp, haredi parties, and Arab factions have complicated coalition negotiations, with disputes over military recruitment conditions and alliance terms creating multiple potential scenarios.

The instability reflects deeper fractures in Israeli politics, where no single bloc commands sufficient Knesset seats to govern independently. The resolution of these tensions will determine whether negotiations produce a functioning government or force new elections.
